From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finway.com>

Subject: Questions after yesterday's demo — connectivity options

Rishi — thanks for the product walkthrough. A few quick clarifying questions as we think about which deployment mode to pick (hosted / dedicated / private):

1) For Private VPC, do you require PrivateLink, or is VPC peering supported for cross-account access? Our infra team prefers peering where possible.
2) What exact outbound egress IPs would Redwood's Private endpoint use if we choose PrivateLink? We need to add allowlist entries in our outgoing firewall and for downstream partners.
3) Does mutual TLS come standard for Private VPC traffic, or is that an add-on? We have strict data-in-transit requirements (mTLS + client certs).

Can we get a short matrix comparing security/latency/cost tradeoffs between PrivateLink vs peering vs dedicated? That will help our procurement and security folks.

Appreciate it — happy to hop back on a call next week.

— Alex
Head of Platform Engineering
FinWay

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions after yesterday's demo — connectivity options

Alex — thanks for the questions, great ones. Quick recap and attachments below. I'll keep this high level and then list the specific network asks for your infra team.

Summary (short):
- Private VPC via PrivateLink: best isolation and simplest firewall footprint for customers with egress allowlists; we expose an AWS PrivateLink endpoint in their account or a cross-account NLB depending on cloud.
- VPC peering: lower latency in many regions and no additional NAT overhead, but it requires peering across accounts and more route table configuration on the customer side. Not supported for every cloud/provider in our Private on-prem pattern.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools in Redwood-managed VPCs, predictable throughput, less network integration but less isolation than full Private VPC.

Attached: a short matrix (redwood-privatelink-vs-peering-matrix.xlsx) and a proposed network diagram (network-diagram-proposal.png).

Network asks for PrivateLink path (if you choose this):
- Customer to provide a CIDR for the PrivateLink NLB if cross-account NLB is needed (recommend small /28 for control plane).
- Egress allowlist: provide full list of destination IPs (we will provide a stable set; expected to be ~4 IPs per region in generally stable ranges).
- TLS: mTLS is supported — we can require client certs on the PrivateLink connection. Provide your KMS/HSM requirements if you need customer-managed keys for cert rotation.
- Ports: 443 for API traffic; 2200 for agent (optional).

Peering path notes:
- We'll need a peering request and the VPC IDs + route tables you want us to modify or accept routes for. Peered networks cannot have overlapping CIDRs.
- If peering, FinWay will manage NAT/egress for calls to third parties — we'll recommend specific NAT configuration.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Infra: share desired path (private-link | peering | dedicated) and your preferred regions.
2) If PrivateLink: send preferred endpoint CIDR and security group baseline.
3) Procurement: Marissa will send draft SOW + pricing options; Ben will share the SLA and capacity lead times.

Would you like a 30-min technical workshop this week with your infra folks and our network engineer? We can make it actionable and lock the allowlist IPs.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Alex — adding procurement + SLA details per Rishi's ask.

High-level commercial notes:
- Private VPC (PrivateLink) has a one-time onboarding fee and an ongoing monthly Private endpoint charge; Dedicated capacity is a monthly committed contract with predictable monthly fees and optional burst credits.
- Typical lead time: Private VPC onboarding (network + security approval) ~3-6 weeks depending on your change window; Dedicated capacity provisioning can be 1-2 weeks if capacity in your region is available.
- We can include an SLA addendum in the SOW for Dedicated.

Immediate next commercial steps:
1) I'll draft a SOW estimate for both PrivateLink and Dedicated options so you can compare TCO.
2) If FinWay prefers peering and it's feasible, we can include peering as an alternative in the SOW, but note peering may require more engineering time from both sides.

I'll attach a draft MUP (mutual action plan) once Rishi confirms the tech path.

— Ben
Senior Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
